description: COSMORA is a team of passionate young innovators exploring Earth science, space technology, and AI. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are taking on The Earth Information Jukebox, transforming NASA Earth data into interactive visualizations and sound. We welcome creative and motivated people with skills in coding, web development, AI, data science, audio engineering, design, and Earth science. No expert experience required—just curiosity, creativity, and teamwork!
summary: COSMORA: Earth Intelligence Lab is a trilingual web workspace for exploring environmental patterns with NASA Earth data. It retrieves monthly temperature, precipitation and other available climate variables from NASA POWER, allowing users to choose locations, review historical periods and compare variables through interactive charts. The lab also brings NASA GIBS satellite imagery into a map-based workspace, with layer and date controls for visual exploration. A grounded analyst explains the retrieved dataset while the interface displays units, coverage, source, retrieval time and data status, helping users distinguish measured data from derived summaries or unavailable results. English, Sinhala and Tamil support makes the experience more accessible to students and communities, including users exploring environmental patterns in Sri Lanka. Current trend descriptions are exploratory and descriptive; the project does not claim formal statistical significance testing or causal attribution.
details:
COSMORA — Earth Intelligence Lab

Project Overview

COSMORA is a NASA-data-powered Earth intelligence workspace designed to help people explore environmental changes using real scientific datasets.

The main component, Earth Intelligence Lab, allows users to investigate historical environmental patterns through NASA POWER data and NASA GIBS satellite imagery.

Main Features

1. NASA POWER Climate Explorer

  • Retrieves monthly historical climate data.
  • Explores temperature, precipitation and other available environmental variables.
  • Supports different study locations, including Sri Lanka and international locations.
  • Displays interactive charts and statistical summaries.
  • Allows users to compare multiple environmental variables.

2. NASA GIBS Imagery Command

  • Displays NASA satellite imagery using interactive maps.
  • Supports different imagery layers and observation dates.
  • Includes side-by-side and swipe-based image comparisons.
  • Shows imagery availability and source information.

3. Sri Lanka Watch

  • Provides Sri Lanka-focused environmental study areas.
  • Helps users explore regional environmental patterns.

4. Grounded AI Earth Analyst

  • Explains retrieved environmental datasets.
  • Separates verified information, derived summaries and interpretations.
  • Reports missing data and scientific limitations instead of inventing measurements.

5. Trilingual Interface

  • English
  • Sinhala
  • Tamil

Technology Stack

The project uses React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express, Recharts, Leaflet, Three.js, React Three Fiber and i18next.

NASA data is accessed through server-side API integrations with caching, error handling and data-provenance reporting.

Innovation and Impact

COSMORA combines climate time-series visualisation, satellite imagery, geographical exploration and an AI-assisted scientific explanation workspace in one platform.

Its goal is to make NASA Earth science data easier to understand and explore, especially for students and communities interested in environmental patterns in Sri Lanka and around the world.

Scientific integrity is an important design consideration. Current trend descriptions are descriptive and exploratory; they do not claim formal statistical significance testing or causal attribution.
